summary: A Santa Fe NF tower on Dead Man's Peak, erected 1933, with a 2002 steel cab per the 2020 chapter report; NHLR-registered 2014; reported staffed in 2020.

facts.design: 30-ft Aermotor MC-24 tower with a 12x12 ft cab; the 2020 chapter report says a steel cab replaced the wooden one in 2002, while the NHLR text still says wooden

events.note: The site has held a fire tower since at least 1913
Erected in 1933 as a 30-ft Aermotor MC-24 with a 12x12 ft wooden cab; the Civilian Conservation Corps built it per the 2020 chapter report
Replaced an earlier wooden platform tower built in the 1920s
Renovation approved under the Accelerated Public Works Program; the tower was rebuilt in the mid-1960s
Roof modified and original nine-pane windows replaced
Evaluated for the 1988 thematic NRHP nomination; found not eligible because of loss of integrity
A contractor built a new steel cab modeled on the wooden one; it was trucked in and set by crane
Registered April 24, 2014; nominated by Scott Waltemeyer
Described as staffed in 2020 (the 2020 report's 'currently staffed') and the only lookout on the Cuba Ranger District

corrections.current: 30-ft Aermotor MC-24 tower with 12x12 wooden cab
corrections.proposed: 30-ft Aermotor MC-24 tower with 12x12 steel cab built in 2002 to replace the wooden cab (per the 2020 chapter report)
corrections.why: The brief lists both the 1933 wooden cab and a 2002 replacement but keeps the wooden design. The 2020 chapter report says the 2002 cab was steel. The NHLR text still describes a wooden cab, so this is a conflict and is flagged.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NHLR page describes a wooden 12-ft cab. The 2020 chapter report, quoting a 2017 account, describes a steel replacement built in 2002. The story follows the later 2020 account and says the register text disagrees.

notes_for_editor: Staffing comes from the 2020 chapter report and may be out of date. Current access is unknown. Cab material conflict is unresolved on the ground.
